papers.title: Learning Realistic Athletic Sprinting Without Demonstrations
papers.authors_short: Wang, Bianco, Tevet, Hicks, Liu, Delp, Fatahalian
papers.venue: SIGGRAPH Asia 2026 (per project page); arXiv cs.GR, 2026-09-10
papers.code_status: Public repos willwng/bolt (NVIDIA Warp simulator) and willwng/msk_envs (RL envs), last pushed Aug 2026; no license file declared (GitHub API, 2026-09-23)
papers.api_title: Learning Realistic Athletic Sprinting Without Demonstrations
papers.core_idea: Bolt, a Warp GPU simulator reproducing OpenSim muscle-tendon dynamics (136 MTUs, elastic tendons), reaches ~1000x real time; FastTD3 trains excitation-space policies from termination rules plus a speed/joint-limit-force reward, yielding a ~10 s 100 m sprint matching sprinter data.
papers.what_to_take: Phase-2 human baseline and engine candidate. Appendices: PPO gave shorter-stride, less dynamic sprints (36-48 h vs ~12 h TD3/SAC); MuJoCo's constraint solver gave unstable gaits, both direct risks for a MyoAssist/PPO sprint build.
papers.left_untested: No device, co-adaptation, 200 m, or fatigue (paper states fatigue is not modelled; maximal output held all race). Narrows O3 by supplying a validated sprinting human and GPU engine; does not close O3. O1, O2, O4 untouched.
papers.feasibility_notes: Trained in under a day on an RTX 6000 PRO; FastTD3 keeps a 26.2M-sample replay buffer on-GPU; check it fits 32 GB. No license declared.

papers.title: Lambda-Hold Control: Human-Like Movement Emerges from a Minimal Task Reward in Predictive Musculoskeletal Simulation
papers.code_status: Project page shows 'Code (TBA)'; not released as of 2026-09-23
papers.api_title: Lambda-Hold Control: Human-Like Movement Emerges from a Minimal Task Reward in Predictive Musculoskeletal Simulation
papers.core_idea: Policy sets per-muscle equilibrium-point thresholds (lambda), held over gait-phase intervals; a stretch-reflex law converts them to excitations. With a velocity-only reward, a 90-muscle SCONE/Hyfydy model learns human-like sprinting (~4 m/s) in about an hour.
papers.what_to_take: Candidate human-side action space for Phase 2: low query rate and reflex-grounded exploration make sprint learning cheap, leaving compute for the device agent. Its speed-only reward pairs naturally with a sprint-time objective.
papers.left_untested: No device, cable actuator, co-adaptation or fatigue; peak speed (~4 m/s) is far below competitive sprinting. Narrows O3 (fast-learning sprinting human) but closes none of O1-O4; MuJoCo/MyoAssist portability untested.
papers.feasibility_notes: About 1 h on an RTX 5070 plus 24-thread CPU. Runs on Hyfydy (separately licensed engine); code unreleased, so expect reimplementation.

papers.title: Experiment-free exoskeleton assistance via learning in simulation [Editor's Note added 27 July 2026]
papers.authors_short: Nature editors; note on Luo, Jiang, Zhang ... Zhou X., Su (2024)
papers.venue: Nature 630:353-359 (2024); Editor's Note dated 2026-07-27 on the article page
papers.code_status: Article's code statement still points to pseudocode only; the note flags data/code availability concerns
papers.api_title: Experiment-free exoskeleton assistance via learning in simulation
papers.core_idea: Nature attached an Editor's Note to Luo et al. 2024 stating that concerns about availability of the data and code supporting its results have been raised, editorial action is pending, and readers should use caution with its results.
papers.what_to_take: Treat Luo 2024 numbers as unverified priors, not targets. Xianlian Zhou, SMAT's last author, co-authored Luo 2024 (publisher metadata), so an open, code-released SMAT reproduction carries unusual evidential weight.
papers.left_untested: The note resolves nothing and no independent re-run was found in this sweep. Raises the stakes of O1 (independent SMAT reproduction) and O2 (open benchmark with matched baselines); closes neither. O3, O4 unaffected.
papers.feasibility_notes: Two-minute read; cite with the Collins critique and Luo reply when framing Phase 1.

papers.title: A roadmap for end-to-end task-agnostic exoskeleton control
papers.code_status: n/a (Perspective)
papers.api_title: A roadmap for end-to-end task-agnostic exoskeleton control
papers.core_idea: Perspective arguing exoskeleton control should move from task classification to end-to-end maps from real-time biological joint-moment estimates to torque; it reviews simulation-trained RL as an alternative limited by sim-to-real gaps and human adaptation that musculoskeletal simulations cannot yet capture.
papers.what_to_take: Use its scale-delay-filter (plus shaping) moment-to-torque map as a named simple baseline family beside velocity-proportional torque; its sim-to-real gap list is a ready threats-to-validity section.
papers.left_untested: A Perspective, not an experiment. It flags human adaptation that simulations miss, which motivates O4 (cross-play against held-out human policies), but it closes none of O1-O4.
papers.feasibility_notes: Paywalled Perspective; publisher page text was readable. No compute.

papers.title: PositiveAssist: Energy-Gated Control for Positive Power Assistance of Exoskeleton in Walking, Running, and Stair Climbing
papers.authors_short: Zhou, Gao, Huang, Lin, Wu, Su
papers.code_status: none found
papers.api_title: PositiveAssist: Energy-Gated Control for Positive Power Assistance of Exoskeleton in Walking, Running, and Stair Climbing
papers.core_idea: Two thigh IMUs estimate hip kinematics and predicted mechanical power; torque is gated to positive-work phases and extension assistance is synthesized from a delayed flexion profile. One fixed parameter set kept >97.8% (walking) and >94.8% (running) of delivered power positive across 0.75-3.5 m/s.
papers.what_to_take: A published, tuning-free power-gated hip controller spanning walking to running speeds: implement it as a second matched simple baseline beside velocity-proportional torque in both the SMAT reproduction and sprint phases.
papers.left_untested: Abstract reports power positivity and transitions for six participants, no metabolic outcome, nothing above 3.5 m/s. Narrows O1's baseline set; closes none of O1-O4 (no simulation, co-adaptation or sprint).
papers.feasibility_notes: Paywalled; abstract gives gating logic but not all constants. Cheap to emulate in simulation from hip velocity and estimated moment.

papers.title: Why inverse simulations overestimate optimal ankle exoskeleton assistance: the role of bi-articular coordination and joint stiffness
papers.venue: Journal of NeuroEngineering and Rehabilitation, 2026-07-21 (preprint Research Square 10.21203/rs.3.rs-9565943/v1)
papers.code_status: Figshare collection linked to the article (contents not inspected)
papers.api_title: Why inverse simulations overestimate optimal ankle exoskeleton assistance: the role of bi-articular coordination and joint stiffness
papers.core_idea: Inverse walking simulations across 0-100% of the biological plantarflexion moment show gastrocnemius bi-articularity caps metabolic savings, and rising assistance cuts ankle stiffness up to 55% via soleus de-recruitment, an impedance loss effort-based costs ignore, inflating simulated optimal assistance.
papers.what_to_take: Effort-only objectives (like activation-reduction rewards) can reward over-assistance. Report joint stiffness or impedance alongside activation when auditing SMAT and when scoring learned sprint assistance.
papers.left_untested: Ankle, walking, inverse (not predictive or RL) simulation; no hip, running or co-adaptation. Adds a validity check for O1's activation metric but closes none of O1-O4.
papers.feasibility_notes: Open access; inverse simulations are cheap and CPU-only. A stiffness metric is easy to add to MyoAssist logging.

papers.title: MetaboliSim: a Python implementation of the Mader model for dynamic and steady-state simulation of muscular energy metabolism
papers.code_status: Open source, AGPL-3.0 (per abstract); repository not inspected
papers.api_title: MetaboliSim: a Python implementation of the Mader model for dynamic and steady-state simulation of muscular energy metabolism
papers.core_idea: First open implementation of the full Mader model: a five-state ODE (phosphate potential, VO2, muscle and blood lactate, glycogen) plus steady-state MLSS equations, verified against published reference outputs and checked on constant-load, step, sprint and running protocols.
papers.what_to_take: A candidate energy/fatigue state for the 200 m task: coupling phosphate potential and lactate to muscle force capacity (our addition, untested) would let assistance matter late in the race, which Bolt ignores.
papers.left_untested: Lumped whole-body energetics with no musculoskeletal or device coupling and no link from metabolic state to muscle force. Narrows O3's physiology gap only; O1, O2, O4 untouched.
papers.feasibility_notes: Pure-Python ODE, negligible cost per step. AGPL-3.0: any distributed derivative must stay AGPL.

papers.title: A Replay-Constrained Simulation Framework for Personalization of Powered Knee--Ankle Prosthesis Controllers
papers.code_status: none found in arXiv record or HTML
papers.api_title: A Replay-Constrained Simulation Framework for Personalization of Powered Knee--Ankle Prosthesis Controllers
papers.core_idea: MuJoCo reproduces prosthetic knee-ankle dynamics while replaying each user's recorded hip kinematics and feedback-based ground reactions instead of modelling neuromuscular control; deep RL personalizes phase-dependent impedance, and simulation predicted hardware outcomes (r=0.96-0.997) in three transfemoral users.
papers.what_to_take: A validation template: report whether simulation rank-orders controllers as hardware (or held-out data) does. Replaying recorded human kinematics is a cheap held-out-partner test for co-adapted device policies.
papers.left_untested: Human is replayed, not adaptive, so no co-adaptation; walking at 0.8 m/s only; prosthesis, not exoskeleton. Narrows O4's evaluation design (held-out recorded humans) without closing it; O1-O3 untouched.
papers.feasibility_notes: CPU MuJoCo simulation of one prosthesis with replayed inputs, so cheap. Needs recorded gait data; no code release found.

papers.title: Simultaneous Forward and Inverse Human-in-the-Loop Optimization
papers.code_status: none found in arXiv record or HTML
papers.api_title: Simultaneous Forward and Inverse Human-in-the-Loop Optimization
papers.core_idea: Learns a forward model from control policy to user outcomes and uses it for active preference queries that infer an individual reward, then optimizes the final policy without extra trials; in simulation it tolerated heterogeneity, noise and nonstationarity and beat mutual-information querying on sample efficiency.
papers.what_to_take: Its simulated-user protocol with explicit nonstationarity is a template for testing device learners against adapting humans, and it treats the reward itself as user-specific and unknown.
papers.left_untested: Low-dimensional HILO with abstract simulated users, not musculoskeletal agents or RL policies; no running or sprint. Tangential to O4 (nonstationary partners); closes none of O1-O4.
papers.feasibility_notes: Bayesian active-learning scale; CPU-trivial. No code link found.

papers.title: Is Inter-Seed Cross-Play Enough? Evaluating the Robustness of Zero-Shot Coordination Algorithms to Implementation Details
papers.code_status: none found in arXiv record or HTML
papers.api_title: Is Inter-Seed Cross-Play Enough? Evaluating the Robustness of Zero-Shot Coordination Algorithms to Implementation Details
papers.core_idea: Proposes cross-implementation cross-play, pairing agents from independently varied implementations rather than only different seeds, and applies it to Other-Play; for that algorithm, standard inter-seed cross-play proved a reasonable proxy for the stricter test.
papers.what_to_take: For O4, build held-out human policies that differ in implementation details (reward weights, network, PPO settings), not only seed, and report both inter-seed and cross-implementation cross-play.
papers.left_untested: Discrete coordination games only; no continuous control, humans or physical coupling. Supplies O4's evaluation protocol but does not close O4; O1-O3 untouched.
papers.feasibility_notes: Evaluation design only; the cost is training several human-policy variants, which GPU batching makes affordable.

papers.title: Optimized Mappings From Biological Hip Moment Estimates to Exoskeleton Torque Can Personalize Assistance Across Users and Generalize Across Tasks
papers.venue: IEEE Transactions on Medical Robotics and Bionics (online 2026-07-13)
papers.code_status: none found
papers.api_title: Optimized Mappings From Biological Hip Moment Estimates to Exoskeleton Torque Can Personalize Assistance Across Users and Generalize Across Tasks
papers.core_idea: Parametrizes moment-based hip control with delay, scaling and shaping terms and tunes it by metabolic HILO in nine subjects across two walking speeds and an incline: personalized maps cut metabolic cost 18.3% versus no exoskeleton, task-agnostic generic maps 8.4%.
papers.what_to_take: Effect sizes for a simple moment-mapping baseline (8-18% metabolic) against which simulated co-adapted controllers should be judged, plus a parametrization easy to reproduce in MyoAssist.
papers.left_untested: Walking only, hardware HILO, no simulation or running. Informs O1's baseline choice but closes none of O1-O4.
papers.feasibility_notes: Needs a joint-moment estimate; in simulation the biological moment is directly available, so this baseline is cheap.

papers.title: Lower limb muscle activity under full and partial towing assistance in sprint running
papers.authors_short: Skujyte, Kamandulis, Genitrini, Satkunskiene et al.
papers.code_status: n/a (experimental study)
papers.api_title: Lower limb muscle activity under full and partial towing assistance in sprint running
papers.core_idea: Thirteen athletes sprinted 30 m unassisted, partially and fully towed by a motorised device: times improved 3.4% and 2.8% through longer strides and flight time and shorter contacts, stride frequency unchanged, while surface EMG of five muscles did not differ.
papers.what_to_take: Real assisted sprinting improved time without reducing muscle activity: score Phase 2 on sprint time, not activation, and use ~3% over 30 m as a plausibility anchor for simulated gains.
papers.left_untested: External towing, not a hip exosuit; 30 m, not 200 m; no simulation. Gives O3 an empirical anchor but does not close it; O1, O2, O4 untouched.
papers.feasibility_notes: Empirical reference only; no compute.

papers.title: Tired Actor: Fatigue-Informed Character Control
papers.authors_short: Zhang, Liu, Niu, Chen, Ma, Gao, Lu, Li
papers.code_status: Abstract says code will be made public; no link found
papers.api_title: Tired Actor: Fatigue-Informed Character Control
papers.core_idea: Injects the Three-Compartment Controller (3CC) fatigue model into physics-based motion-imitation policies so characters have finite, depleting capacity, then analyses how fatigue changes the naturalness, scalability and robustness of learned control.
papers.what_to_take: A tested way to put a fatigue state inside an RL policy's dynamics and observations; 3CC is a lighter alternative to the Mader model for the 200 m human.
papers.left_untested: General motion imitation, not sprint racing; no device or co-adaptation. Narrows O3's fatigue gap in method only; O1, O2, O4 untouched.
papers.feasibility_notes: 3CC adds a few states per actuator, negligible cost. Code not yet released.

papers.title: Ensuring Interaction Safety in Multitask Exoskeleton Control: A Simulation-Trained Variable Impedance Framework
papers.authors_short: Ma, Li, Zhai, Han, Meng, Xia, Cheng
papers.code_status: Simulation dataset via anonymous link (per paper HTML); training code not found
papers.api_title: Ensuring Interaction Safety in Multitask Exoskeleton Control: A Simulation-Trained Variable Impedance Framework
papers.core_idea: PPO synthesizes human muscle activations in simulation while the exoskeleton directly compensates biological joint torques; the data train an instruction-plus-proprioception policy predicting reference trajectories and variable impedance for nine tasks, with Lyapunov-bounded stiffness, cutting metabolic cost on hardware versus baselines.
papers.what_to_take: A non-co-adaptive alternative: generate assisted-human data with a fixed 'exo cancels biological torque' rule, then distil. A useful ablation arm against staged co-adaptation.
papers.left_untested: Exo rule is fixed torque compensation, not co-adapted; abstract reports no sprint or partner-transfer test. Adds a comparison arm relevant to O2 but closes none of O1-O4.
papers.feasibility_notes: PPO musculoskeletal data generation fits a one-GPU budget; the anonymous dataset link may expire.

papers.title: Simulation of Adaptive Running With Flexible Sports Prosthesis Using Reinforcement Learning of Hybrid-Link System
papers.venue: IEEE Robotics and Automation Letters (online 2026-05-15); arXiv 2026-04-10
papers.code_status: none found in arXiv record or HTML
papers.api_title: Simulation of Adaptive Running With Flexible Sports Prosthesis Using Reinforcement Learning of Hybrid-Link System
papers.core_idea: Couples a whole-body transtibial-amputee model with a Piece-wise Constant Strain model of a leaf-spring running prosthesis; RL with motion-capture imitation generates running under several virtual prosthesis stiffnesses, and cost of transport agrees with prior reports.
papers.what_to_take: Shows RL running simulations can sweep a device parameter (stiffness) and report energetic trade-offs; a model for sweeping exosuit cable stiffness and slack in Phase 2.
papers.left_untested: Imitation-anchored, so the human cannot re-coordinate freely; passive device; no sprint-time objective or co-adaptation. Narrows O3 methodologically without closing it; O1, O2, O4 untouched.
papers.feasibility_notes: Soft-rigid hybrid dynamics are custom, not a MuJoCo drop-in. Concept transfers; code not found.

papers.title: Reflex-Informed Neuromuscular Reinforcement Learning for Muscle-Driven Locomotion
papers.authors_short: Zhou, Zhang, Ma, Cao, Xie, Zhang
papers.code_status: none found in arXiv record or HTML
papers.api_title: Reflex-Informed Neuromuscular Reinforcement Learning for Muscle-Driven Locomotion
papers.core_idea: A fixed phase-dependent reflex controller drives the muscles while an RL policy outputs four residual parameters modulating hip-swing, knee-support and ankle-propulsion reflex gains and thresholds; gait is more accurate, symmetric and consistent, and stays robust to weakness and perturbations without retraining.
papers.what_to_take: A second low-dimensional, physiology-grounded human controller (4 actions) to compare with lambda-hold and with SMAT's full-excitation PPO human; a candidate held-out partner family for O4.
papers.left_untested: Nominal walking only; no running, sprint, device or co-adaptation. Supplies candidate partner policies for O4 but closes none of O1-O4.
papers.feasibility_notes: Four-dimensional residual action space trains cheaply; simulator and code availability not confirmed.

papers.title: Unified comparison of spinal locomotion control architectures in neuromechanical simulations
papers.code_status: Authors state the framework and controllers are publicly shared; URL not checked
papers.api_title: Unified comparison of spinal locomotion control architectures in neuromechanical simulations
papers.core_idea: Implements reflex, CPG-reflex, synergy and CPG-reflex-synergy controllers in one neuromechanical framework with shared models and optimisation: reflex and CPG-reflex-synergy best match human gait, and CPG-reflex-synergy is most versatile across speeds and slopes.
papers.what_to_take: A model for O2's design (same body, optimiser and metrics across several controllers) and for its caveat that results compare implementations, not biological hypotheses.
papers.left_untested: Walking controllers only; no devices, RL, running or co-adaptation. Methodological precedent for O2 but closes none of O1-O4.
papers.feasibility_notes: Reflex/CPG optimisation is CPU-bound and suits the 64-core EPYC. CC-BY preprint, not peer reviewed.

papers.title: The effects of muscle fibre type distribution on gait biomechanics: A predictive simulation study
papers.code_status: none found in bioRxiv record
papers.api_title: The effects of muscle fibre type distribution on gait biomechanics: A predictive simulation study
papers.core_idea: A muscle model with separate slow- and fast-twitch fibres inside predictive simulation (1.0-4.5 m/s) shows more slow fibres lower cost of transport in walking, while in running the effect on cost and stride parameters reverses around a threshold speed.
papers.what_to_take: A sprinting human needs fast-fibre physiology; this gives a two-fibre muscle formulation to weigh before trusting single-fibre Hill models at sprint speeds.
papers.left_untested: Tops out at 4.5 m/s; no sprint, device, RL or fatigue. Narrows O3's physiology question marginally; closes none of O1-O4.
papers.feasibility_notes: Two-fibre muscles are not native to MuJoCo; porting needs custom actuator code. CC-BY preprint.

papers.title: MuJoCoUni:Persistent Batched Runtime Primitives for MuJoCo
papers.code_status: Open-source pip package mujoco-uni; benchmark repo unilabsim/mujoco_uni_bench (per paper)
papers.api_title: MuJoCoUni:Persistent Batched Runtime Primitives for MuJoCo
papers.core_idea: A downstream MuJoCo distribution adding a C++ BatchEnvPool that owns per-environment models and per-thread data workers for stateful batched stepping, sparse resets, domain randomization and batched sensor queries, while leaving MuJoCo's solver, contact and integrator semantics unchanged.
papers.what_to_take: A CPU-side throughput lever for the 64-core EPYC that keeps exact upstream MuJoCo semantics, useful for the SMAT reproduction, where GPU-port numerical differences would confound comparison.
papers.left_untested: No musculoskeletal benchmark in the abstract; speedups for MyoAssist-scale models unknown. Supports O1/O2 infrastructure; closes none of O1-O4.
papers.feasibility_notes: pip install mujoco-uni; check compatibility with MyoAssist's pinned MuJoCo version first.

papers.title: Beyond Heuristics: A Standardized Real2Sim Pipeline for Physical Human Robot Interaction in Human-in-the-Loop Simulation
papers.authors_short: Yang, Wang, Tan, Chan et al.
papers.code_status: Project page linked in paper HTML; code not confirmed
papers.api_title: Beyond Heuristics: A Standardized Real2Sim Pipeline for Physical Human Robot Interaction in Human-in-the-Loop Simulation
papers.core_idea: Identifies a 6-DoF viscoelastic pelvis-strap interface (12 stiffness/damping parameters) per subject with CMA-ES at a 'safe and comfortable' operating point; shared priors calibrate a new subject by refining 5 parameters, and calibrated interfaces yield accurate gait adaptation in a human digital twin.
papers.what_to_take: Soft human-device interfaces should be identified, not guessed: model exosuit strap and cuff compliance explicitly when imposing realistic cable-actuator limits in Phase 2.
papers.left_untested: Overground balance assistant, not an exosuit; no RL device policy, running or co-adaptation. Narrows O3's interface-realism component only; O1, O2, O4 untouched.
papers.feasibility_notes: CMA-ES identification needs subject data; without it, use published parameter ranges as priors.

cluster_lessons: The April-September 2026 frontier moved on the human side, not the device side: two demonstration-free sprinting musculoskeletal controllers appeared (Bolt 2609.11083; lambda-hold 2608.17030), but neither includes a device, fatigue or a 200 m race.

Engine and optimiser choices matter for sprint realism: Bolt's appendices report that MuJoCo constraint-solver joint limits destabilised sprint gaits and that PPO produced shorter-stride, less dynamic sprints than TD3/SAC at roughly three times the wall-clock. A MyoAssist + PPO Phase 2 inherits both risks until tested.

Reproducibility pressure intensified: Nature added an Editor's Note (27 July 2026) to Luo et al. 2024 over data and code availability. Publisher metadata lists Xianlian Zhou, SMAT's last author, as a Luo 2024 co-author, which makes an open, independent SMAT reproduction more consequential.

Simple hip controllers are published, strong and cheap to emulate: energy-gated positive-power assistance (PositiveAssist, walking to 3.5 m/s running) and optimized moment-to-torque maps (Powell 2026; Shepherd et al. roadmap). Learned co-adapted controllers should be compared against these, not only against zero torque.

Effort-only outcomes mislead: inverse simulations overestimate optimal assistance because effort costs ignore the loss of joint stiffness (Luis 2026), and towed sprinting improved 30 m time ~3% with unchanged EMG (Skujyte 2026). Score sprint assistance by time and kinematics, with activation as secondary.

Simulation validity can be tested by rank agreement: the replay-constrained prosthesis framework predicted which controllers performed best on hardware. Rank-order agreement with held-out data is a cheap validity metric for the programme.

No paper in the window evaluated device controllers against held-out human policies. Zero-shot-coordination work supplies the protocol (inter-seed vs cross-implementation cross-play), and replaying recorded humans supplies a data-driven variant.

Fatigue and energetics are missing from every sprint simulation found; open building blocks now exist (MetaboliSim's Mader model, AGPL; the 3CC model used by Tired Actor) but nobody has coupled them to a muscle-driven sprinter.
occupied_claims: Demonstration-free, muscle-driven full 100 m sprint from an open GPU (Warp) simulator implementing OpenSim muscle dynamics at ~1000x real time, validated against sprinter data (Wang et al., 2609.11083, SIGGRAPH Asia 2026).
Human-like sprinting from a minimal velocity reward in about an hour via equilibrium-point (lambda) actions and reflex recruitment (Lee, Lee, Ahn, 2608.17030).
Off-policy RL (TD3/SAC) beats PPO for muscle-driven sprinting, and MuJoCo's constraint solver degrades sprint gait versus force-based joint limits (Bolt appendices, 2609.11083).
Replay-constrained simulation (recorded human kinematics plus simulated device) ranks personalized prosthesis controllers consistently with hardware (Le et al., 2607.22858).
Tuning-free, positive-power-gated hip assistance across walking and running speeds from two thigh IMUs (PositiveAssist, TMECH 2026).
Delay-scale-shape moment-to-torque maps personalized by HILO, 18.3% vs 8.4% generic metabolic reduction (Powell et al., TMRB 2026).
Inverse simulations overestimate optimal ankle assistance because effort costs ignore stiffness loss (Luis et al., JNER 2026).
Towing assistance improves sprint time without lowering EMG (Skujyte et al., Sports Biomechanics 2026).
First open, verified implementation of the full Mader energy model including sprint protocols (MetaboliSim, 2606.08366).
Fatigue (3CC) integrated into physics-based character control (Tired Actor, 2608.03528).
Cross-implementation cross-play as a stricter zero-shot-coordination test (Wolski et al., 2608.03644).
Controlled comparison of reflex, CPG and synergy locomotion controllers in one neuromechanical framework (Ton and Song, bioRxiv 2026).
open_gaps: O1 remains open: no independent reproduction of SMAT, SMAT-ext or UniExo was found through 2026-09-23, and no paper compares a co-adapted exo policy with velocity-proportional, power-gated (PositiveAssist-style) or moment-mapped baselines under a reward-matched zero-torque control.

O2 remains open: no open, GPU-batched, staged human-device co-adaptation benchmark with matched baselines appeared. Bolt (GPU musculoskeletal, no device) and the known Assistax are the nearest pieces.

O3 remains open and untouched by any window paper: no simulated hip-exosuit assistance of sprinting at all, let alone 200 m sprint time under cable-actuator limits. Sprint simulators omit fatigue (Bolt states this) and devices; the only 2026 empirical anchor found is towing (~3% over 30 m).

O4 remains open: no cross-play or partner-transfer evaluation of co-adapted device controllers against held-out human policies. Protocols exist (inter-seed vs cross-implementation cross-play; replayed recorded humans) but were never applied to human-device co-adaptation.

Prerequisite for O3 in MuJoCo: whether MyoAssist/MuJoCo can produce realistic sprints at all, given Bolt's report that MuJoCo constraint-solver joint limits destabilised sprint gaits; a short feasibility test should precede Phase 2.
Untested whether staged co-adaptation stays stable with off-policy learners (TD3/SAC), which Bolt found superior for sprinting, versus SMAT's PPO.
No musculoskeletal sprinter couples an energetics or fatigue state (Mader, 3CC) to muscle force capacity; without it a 200 m objective reduces to a 100 m-style maximal effort.
unverifiable: 'Predictive Timing Optimization of Hip Exoskeleton Assistance in Running' (Foggetti, Moncelli, Shafi, Trigili, Crea; BioRob 2026, 10.1109/BioRob66782.2026.11681147): title and venue confirmed via Crossref, but no abstract in Crossref or OpenAlex and IEEE Xplore blocked automated access. Content not assessed; possibly relevant to O3.

'A Co-Simulation Platform for Closed-Loop Evaluation of Human-Exoskeleton Control Strategies' (Shakourisalim et al.; BioRob 2026, 10.1109/BioRob66782.2026.11681699): title confirmed via Crossref; abstract inaccessible; possibly relevant to O2.

'A Comparison of Four Methods for Predictive Musculoskeletal Simulations of Human Walking' (Denayer, De Pauw, Verstraten; BioRob 2026, 10.1109/BioRob66782.2026.11681138): title confirmed via Crossref; abstract inaccessible; possibly relevant to simulation-reproducibility audits.

'Continual Reinforcement Learning for Walking Control in a Musculoskeletal Simulation of Hemiparesis' (Jones, Young, Uhlrich, Pilarski, Dalrymple; BioRob 2026, 10.1109/BioRob66782.2026.11681004): title confirmed via Crossref; abstract inaccessible.

'Finite-Time Robust Control for Bowden Cable-Driven Exoskeletons With Time-Varying Cable Configurations' (IEEE TCST 2026, 10.1109/TCST.2026.3713361): title seen in a Crossref search; the DOI record request failed and OpenAlex has no abstract. Possibly relevant to cable-actuator limits.
bioRxiv 10.64898/2026.03.30.715312 ('Can predictive simulations provide insights for personalizing assistive wearable device design?') is marked WITHDRAWN in v2 (2026-08-06); do not cite.
A web-search summary of the Luo reply mentions 'Zhou et al. (2025, ~20% during running)' for learning-in-simulation; not verified and outside the window.
